how_ranked: Ranked by (1) how many of the 24 blind players hit the problem it fixes, (2) how many players reach the place in a first session (everyone starts in Times Square; then Grand Central 7, Chinatown 6, Joe's Pizza 5, Brooklyn Bridge 5, the apartment 4, Wall Street 4, the Met 3), and (3) effort. Ideas come from the three design audits (backlog refs are row numbers in design/backlog.json).

fix_first.title: Make the people answer
fix_first.what: City locals reply to chat in context (a question about Queens gets 'Take the 7 to Flushing'; a missing place gets an honest 'not on the map yet'), real players carry a visible badge, and a typed line shows who heard it.
fix_first.evidence: 16 of 24 found the people canned; 6 left after a chat line nobody answered; only 1 friendship formed, from the one question asked in company.

fix_first.title: Say where things are
fix_first.what: Name every place on the map without hovering, label the toolbar icons, and give Rosa's tour a 'things to do near you' list that walks you there.
fix_first.evidence: 13 hit unlabelled icons; 7 asked for things that already exist (Central Park, SoHo, Adel's cart, Flag Roll Call); 16 of 30 rooms were never visited.

fix_first.title: Shorten the first walk
fix_first.what: A bigger Skip Intro, skip on replay, a wider swipe window for trackpads and slow hands, and an OMNY tap beside the swipe (the joke stays).
fix_first.evidence: 14 found the swipe finicky (9 failed twice or more); 10 said the intro ran long; 5 caught MetroCard vs OMNY.

fix_first.title: Confirm what already works
fix_first.what: 'You joined the Dance Jam', a toast for level-up coins, Take a Walk counting any walk, a running tally in Carb-Jitsu.
fix_first.evidence: 6 thought the Dance Jam was broken; 4 saw Take a Walk never tick; jiwoo quit Carb-Jitsu with no tally.

fix_first.title: Wire the moments that are built
fix_first.what: Rowboat, squirrel, love locks, life ring, opening bell and Washington's pose exist but no object opens them; register their 18 stamps. Give the Met doors and the dead arrows something to do.
fix_first.evidence: Design audit (parks and downtown); lukas, maya and darnell clicked the dead doors and arrow.

fix_first.title: Close the safety gaps parents named
fix_first.what: Filter 'real name' and 'what school' style questions, move 'Use a Photo' after the other options and say where the photo goes, and plan a friends-only or preset chat mode for parents and classes.
fix_first.evidence: All 3 parents and teachers flagged the checkbox age gate and the selfie-first option (used by 0 of 24); a real-name-and-school question passed the filter with a 15-year-old in the room.

fix_first.title: Keep the memorial quiet
fix_first.what: No stamp chime or '+25 XP' at the 9/11 pools, and move the two jokes away from them.
fix_first.evidence: Design audit; angie: 'quiet, factual, no jokes, a white rose. This is what made me trust the place.'

fix_first.title: Fix the facts the experts caught
fix_first.what: Times Sq-42 St lines, the intro ride and its 13-line car strip, the Bull at Bowling Green, the Whispering Gallery's level, the 7 on the map, Rockefeller Center's lines, the ferry 'is free' line, '$.99' slices, the opal clock as 'reputedly'.
fix_first.evidence: 5 to 1 catches each from marcus, sam, nora, tunde, priya, linda, wei, lukas, jiwoo.

top.title: Locals with small favors
top.what: Now and then a local asks a 10 to 30 second favor (take our photo, hold my coffee, which way to the A?) and reacts to what you hold ('Fold it.' to a slice).
top.evidence: 16 found the people static; the one real conversation made the round's only friendship.

top.title: Wait for the train
top.what: Countdown sign, headlights in the tunnel, the gust, riders off first, 'stand clear', then the ride, on a shared clock so everyone on the platform boards the same train.
top.evidence: 5 called the ride 'a title card plus a station name'; sam and lukas wanted the subway as a system.

top.title: The city reacts to your feet
top.where: Wall Street, the Battery, Central Park, Times Square
top.what: Pigeons, gulls and leaf piles burst up as you walk through, bigger with a crowd, from positions the game already shares.
top.evidence: Pigeons were the 3rd most-named true NYC detail (12); marcus found Times Square 'empty and clean'.

top.title: Order, wait, eat
top.what: One pattern everywhere: order from picture chips, watch it made, take it, and finish it with one verb (fold the slice, mustard squiggle, stab the boba straw, sip before you bite the dumpling).
top.evidence: Carts were the 2nd most-named true NYC detail (19), yet marcus got 'no slice in my hand, no fold, no bite' and wei 'click, one line, coins'.

top.title: Cards become verbs
top.what: A click makes your New Yorker do something to the thing, and the fact arrives inside the action (the counter guy says it, the cup sleeve prints it); every fact lands in a 'City Notes' page of the Stamp Book to reread.
top.evidence: 10 flagged fact cards; ron wanted to reread them; aiko wanted one short line and a picture.

top.title: Meet me at the clock
top.what: Pick an online friend, they get 'Meet me at the clock'; when you're both at the booth the clock faces glow and chime.
top.evidence: Grand Central delighted all 7 visitors but the clock is a card.

top.title: Whispering Gallery for two
top.what: Stand in opposite corners; what one types only the other hears.
top.evidence: nora: 'I hoped for the real trick'; millie and ellen loved the solo whisper.

top.title: Catch the 5:52
top.what: Buy at the ticket windows, wait under the board until the track posts, everyone rushes, the conductor punches your ticket.
top.evidence: millie: 'I wanted to see trains and times, or pick a train home.'

top.title: Bang on the pipe
top.what: The radiator clanks in heat season; bang the pipe and the neighbor upstairs bangs back in rhythm. Rosa knocks once a day.
top.evidence: The apartment delighted all 4 visitors; millie confirmed the heat-season facts.

top.title: Bike lane!
top.what: Stand on the bike half: two bell dings, a cyclist grows out of the distance, yells and swerves; more people in the lane bring more bikes.
top.evidence: 5 visited the bridge; darnell found it static.

top.title: Walk into Brooklyn
top.what: The dead right arrow becomes a walk: boards scroll, the arch passes overhead, tourists stop for photos in your path.
top.evidence: darnell: 'looked like a way out, did nothing'; 4 asked for Brooklyn.

top.title: Tower viewers you play
top.where: Empire State, Liberty Island, the High Line, Sky Deck
top.what: Drop a coin, the shutter clacks open, three pictured things to spot before it snaps shut; a collection per viewer, and friends' pins in calm mode.
top.evidence: gabi and maya: 'just a picture'.

top.title: The Met opens its doors
top.what: Climb the steps, a guard hands you today's sticker; on the top step a red carpet rolls out for a photo walk.
top.evidence: lukas and maya: 'the big doors do nothing and there is no interior'.

top.title: A Big Board you can play
top.what: Step up and call the market one LED row at a time; Bull Market Brad heckles.
top.evidence: tyler and lukas: 'a popup of prices I cannot trade'; priya loved the ticker jokes.

top.title: Carb-Jitsu, finished
top.what: A running tally, real players matched before a local fills the seat, a rematch button, and a board in Times Square that says a table is waiting.
top.evidence: All 4 players loved it; the 7 who played any game stayed longest; jiwoo quit with no tally; 3 minded the bot; diego found it at action 60.

top.title: Sal's dog
top.what: Tongs to fish out a dog, your own mustard squiggle, Sal's eyebrows, and he learns your usual.
top.evidence: Every player starts beside Sal's cart; the welcome gift there was named fun by 4.

top.title: The living statue
top.what: A painted-green Lady Liberty frozen on a crate: tip her a coin and she shifts; try emote combos until she cracks up.
top.evidence: marcus wanted crowds and costumed characters in an 'empty and clean' Times Square.

top.title: Shake the snow globe
top.what: Drag to shake, let the snow settle on a random scene to collect (a golden pigeon is rare), keep it or put it back.
top.evidence: Shops felt like menus (wei, linda, diego).

top.title: The hot sauce dare
top.what: Each red drop raises a heat meter; at three you steam and hop, and Adel says 'I told you.'
top.evidence: wei: 'white sauce / hot sauce is correct'; marcus never found the cart.

top.title: The ferry crossing
top.what: Ticket, security bin, gangway, horn, gulls, the statue growing, a photo when she's centered, the rope throw; the free orange Staten Island Ferry beside it.
top.evidence: gabi's dream path ended there; today it's a 3-second card one way and a teleport back; the dock local wrongly says the ferry is free.

top.title: Photos worth sending
top.where: The Battery, Liberty Island, photo booths
top.what: Pinch the statue between your fingers, line your foam torch up with hers, and get a postcard to share.
top.evidence: 5 wanted share tools; gabi wanted to show her crown to her trip group.

top.title: Decorating that feels good
top.what: Preview before buying, a tray that doesn't cover the room, free furniture left on a curb once a day, and Mango the cat who sits on whatever you placed last.
top.evidence: chloe and diego: items spawn at your feet, the tray covers half the room, the catalog reopens.

top.title: Your Block: the bodega and the stoop
top.what: Papi's bodega (the art is already painted, cat included): order a chopped cheese, 'salt pepper ketchup?', pet Mango; sit on the stoop with neighbors.
top.evidence: 13 wanted a place from their own New York; no bodega exists.

top.title: Hail a cab
top.what: Raise your arm as lit cabs stream past, ride with the back-seat TV, pick the avenue or the FDR, tip on the screen, share it with friends.
top.evidence: gabi 'hoped to ride it'; 8 named yellow cabs as true NYC.

top.title: A living map
top.what: Friends' faces pinned where they are, crowd dots, a sparkle where something is happening, names always on.
top.evidence: maya landed on the Empire State aiming for Central Park; sam: 'just a teleport menu'.

big_bets.title: Beyond Manhattan
big_bets.what: Start with Queens on the 7 (Flushing or Jackson Heights), then Harlem and a Brooklyn block; label the gap honestly until then.
big_bets.evidence: 13 wanted a place from their own life; 10 noticed a missing borough (Queens 6, Brooklyn 4, Bronx 2, Staten Island 2); natives scored NYC feel 6.2 and recommend 4.6, the lowest of any group.

big_bets.title: A game in the first minute
big_bets.what: A short skill game reachable from Times Square in the first minute (Rush Hour Run on the platform, Carb-Jitsu on the red steps), and arrow-key walking for people who reach for it.
big_bets.evidence: 11 wanted something to do early; tyler left at 25 actions over 'nothing to get good at'; mini-game players stayed 64 actions against 39.

big_bets.title: Parent and classroom mode
big_bets.what: Friends-only or preset-phrase chat a parent can turn on, a private class room, and a For Parents page.
big_bets.evidence: frank: 'not alone yet'; linda: 'not for my class'; kevin: 'cautiously yes'.

big_bets.title: Easier to read
big_bets.what: A simpler-English mode and translations, a text-size setting, and short picture-led lines.
big_bets.evidence: aiko left on 'too much English'; gabi stumbled on idioms; ron and ellen on small text.
